clue.text: Confine and let out about a hundred — magic figure!

parts.note: to confine is to pen, as with sheep

indicators.note: about here means wrapped around the other piece, as a container
let out suggests the letters of the word let are freed and rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A conjuror shuts something in, releases it, and points to a mystic symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LET into TLE, and 'about' places A plus C (a hundred) inside it to make TACLE after PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentacle is a five-pointed star used as a symbol in magic rituals.

clue.text: I'm getting opera rewritten for the big stores

indicators.note: rewritten says the letters of the preceding words are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is having an opera recomposed to suit large department stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges the letters of I'M and OPERA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is the plural of emporium, a large shop or trading centre.

clue.text: Possible starters include one, Faithless Lady

indicators.note: include asks for the piece for one to go inside the other word
possible starters means the word starters could be arranged differently

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A list of runners in a race, one of them a woman who has broken faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' puts I (one) into STARTERS, and 'Possible' rearranges the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitress is a woman who betrays her trust, a female traitor.

clue.text: As attractive as some tunes — or trick questions?

explanation.surface: A comparison of appealing melodies with puzzling quiz questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy tune is easily remembered and appealing, and a catchy question is tricky, designed to catch someone out.

clue.text: Not a shocking luxury, it's assumed, for one enjoying retirement

definitions.text: Not a shocking luxury, it's assumed, for one enjoying retirement

parts.words: Not a shocking luxury, it's assumed, for one enjoying retirement
parts.note: the retirement is going to bed, and the luxury runs on mains power that one hopes gives no shock

explanation.surface: A pensioner's treat is thought to be quite unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work but means going to bed, and 'shocking' hints at electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a heated bedcover powered by mains supply, a comfort for someone heading to bed.

clue.text: Bard's lowest part

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's lowliest role in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, and the base of anything is its lowest part.

clue.text: Exclude three articles of material

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them
the articles a, the and a, in that order

explanation.surface: A legal ruling bars three items of cloth from a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' are the grammatical ones: indefinite A and definite THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen fabric, often used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Bond leads the game — what an artist!

indicators.note: leads means comes in front of the next piece in the answer

parts.note: a tie is a bond or link
polo is the game played on horseback

explanation.surface: James Bond is ahead in a match, and an onlooker exclaims at the talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy but is simply a tie. Tiepolo was an 18th-century Venetian painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was a Venetian painter famous for frescoes.

clue.text: Beaten side made to provide this pie-filling?

definitions.text: Beaten side made to provide this pie-filling?

parts.words: Beaten side made to provide this pie-filling?
parts.note: an idiom for thrashing a team is to chop them up finely, like the filling of a Christmas pie

explanation.surface: A defeated team is turned into the stuffing for pies.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'make X of' a side is to beat it heavily; the filling of British Christmas pies of dried fruit and suet has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat is a sweet filling of dried fruit and spices, and making it of opponents means thrashing them.

clue.text: One choosing to work so much abroad

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
tant is French for so much, a word from abroad

explanation.surface: A person who decides to go and work a great deal overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' signals a foreign word: French TANT, so much.
explanation.definitionFit: An optant is a person who makes a choice, especially of nationality.

clue.text: National leader of the EEC

explanation.surface: A country's head of state also heads the Common Market.
explanation.walkthrough: The EEC was the European Economic Community, so the first word of its full name leads it.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a country on the continent is one, and the word is the first of the three spelt out by the initials EEC.

clue.text: Note, for a whim, the name of Peacock's Castle

explanation.surface: Someone notes a fanciful idea, the name of a castle belonging to a man called Peacock.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Love Peacock wrote the satirical novel Crotchet Castle (1831).
explanation.definitionFit: It is a quarter note in music, an old word for a fanciful notion, and the title of Peacock's satirical novel.

clue.text: Cast, we hear, for top position in the state

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by its sound when spoken

parts.note: cast means thrown, as a stone is

explanation.surface: Actors are chosen, we're told, for the highest role in a government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like actors but is the past tense of throw.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat of a monarch stands for the sovereign's supreme position in a realm.

clue.text: Hold direction for harbour

parts.note: to have is to hold or possess
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A ship keeps its course towards port.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a sheltered port or anchorage where ships are safe.

clue.text: Not a genuine sort of canter

definitions.text: Not a genuine sort of canter

parts.words: Not a genuine sort of canter
parts.note: a canter here is not a horse's gait but one who speaks cant, pious insincere talk

explanation.surface: A horse's gait that is somehow fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canter' suggests riding, but one who cants spouts sanctimonious humbug.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who professes virtues they lack is a sham, a person given to sanctimonious cant.

clue.text: Important event that marks one's progress by the way

definitions.text: that marks one's progress by the way

explanation.surface: A key occasion that shows how far someone has come along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a significant stage in life, and literally a roadside marker showing the distance travelled.

clue.text: Peter first supports young Cratchit as a musician

indicators.note: in a down clue, supports means placed below the other piece

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the young son of Bob Cratchit in Dickens's A Christmas Carol
Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up
first is abbreviated 1st, read here as IST

explanation.surface: A man named Peter is first to help a Dickens boy become a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' in a down clue puts PAN + IST under TIM. 1ST is read with the figure 1 as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A timpanist plays the kettledrums in an orchestra.

clue.text: Conduct a bridge partnership in the region

indicators.note: in says the partnership sits inside the word for the region

parts.note: a tract is a region or stretch of land
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Organising a bridge pair to play somewhere locally.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the players sit as North-South and East-West pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to carry it out or conduct it.

clue.text: Ban one who writes for money?

parts.note: a pro, or professional, works for pay
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: Should a paid writer be prohibited?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ban' looks like a person's name, but it is the definition: the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe something is to forbid or outlaw it.

clue.text: Wine of gold taken in Oslo perhaps with duck

indicators.note: taken in says gold is placed inside the rearranged letters
Oslo perhaps means the city's name could be spelt in another order

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A gold-coloured wine is drunk in Norway's capital alongside roast duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OSLO as OLOS, and 'taken in' puts OR between OL and OS; O (a cricket duck, zero runs) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, full-bodied type of sherry.

clue.text: Some of them met an old worker

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the people one encountered were elderly labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmet is an archaic or dialect word for an ant, the classic worker insect.

clue.text: He makes one cross from time to time

definitions.text: He makes one cross from time to time

parts.words: He makes one cross from time to time
parts.note: the cross is not anger but the X marked on a ballot paper at each election

explanation.surface: A man who periodically annoys someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' suggests making someone angry; it is the X put on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter marks an X on the ballot paper whenever there is an election.

clue.text: Cause of interference when Old Possum's pets hold it up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole is read from bottom to top
hold means the pets enclose the following word

parts.note: T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats

explanation.surface: Eliot's felines cause a disturbance by holding something aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' puts IT inside CATS to give CITATS; 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Static electricity causes crackling interference on radio reception.

clue.text: Like the devilish extremity of about 50 witches

indicators.note: about says the group of witches goes round the number

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Around fifty witches share the Devil's hoofed foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately' but places COVEN around L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil is pictured with split hooves, so his feet are divided in two.

clue.text: Edentate 19 ruined a tree

parts.note: the answer to 19 across is an old word for an ant

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of a tree are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Some toothless creature, ants included, has wrecked a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges A TREE as EATER. Edentates are toothless mammals such as sloths and armadillos.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect-eating mammal has no teeth and belongs to the edentate order.

clue.text: Metal vessel for eucalyptus

parts.note: iron is a metal
a bark or barque is a sailing ship

explanation.surface: A metal ship is fitted out to carry gum trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironbarks are Australian gum trees with hard, furrowed bark.

clue.text: Say, are you match players? How many?

definitions.text: Say, are you match players? How many?

parts.words: Say, are you match players? How many?
parts.note: a rugby union match puts two teams of fifteen on the field, so the question asks the total

explanation.surface: A spectator asks whether some people are in the team and how many there are.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union has fifteen players a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Two rugby union sides of fifteen give this total on the pitch.

clue.text: It goes wrong for Meredith's hero

indicators.note: goes wrong says the letters of it goes are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something fails for the leading man in a Meredith story.
explanation.walkthrough: George Meredith's novel The Egoist (1879) centres on the self-absorbed Sir Willoughby Patterne.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Meredith's novel is a self-centred man.

clue.text: I act strangely, become uncommunicative

indicators.note: strangely says the words I act are put in an odd order

parts.note: to turn is to become, as milk turns sour

explanation.surface: An actor admits behaving oddly and going quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges I ACT to TACI.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person says little and is reserved in speech.
